A1.justification: Both are complete, readable versions of the SPORTU paper, including Appendices A–Q. Matching text, tables, figures and appendix material support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V3 reports original evaluations of four text LLMs and fourteen video MLLMs, including benchmark scores, human ratings, multi-angle comparisons and error analyses.

after.justification: V4 retains these original empirical evaluations in the main results and appendices. Tables 1–4 report model accuracy and explanation-evaluation results.

M1.justification: The benchmark design, annotation procedures and three prompting strategies remain unchanged. No model architecture, objective or inference component is introduced or revised.

E1.justification: Both retain 900 SPORTU-text questions and 1,701 SPORTU-video clips with 12,048 QA pairs, including the same difficulty levels and multi-angle scenarios. Revised sourcing language does not establish added or replaced evaluation data.

E2.justification: The same four text LLMs and fourteen video MLLMs participate in the corresponding main and appendix comparisons. Model and prompting-comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: Model versions and sizes, frame inputs, temperature, prompting settings, evaluation metrics and human-evaluation samples remain unchanged in Section 4 and Appendices J–L. The sourcing rewrite does not establish a changed evaluation procedure.

E4.justification: Both contain the same multi-angle analysis, question-type and difficulty breakdowns, prompting case studies, metric–human correlations and error analyses in Appendices D–I, M and Q.

E5.justification: Point-estimate reporting and the Pearson-correlation analysis are unchanged. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Main and appendix result tables, plots and qualitative examples retain the same results. Examples include GPT-4o's 71.00% text accuracy under five-shot CoT in Table 2 and Qwen2-VL-72B's 70.94% video accuracy under X→Y in Table 3.

T1.justification: Neither version introduces formal theoretical results or proofs. Prompting notation and definitions of the multi-angle correctness categories remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same benchmark contributions and claims about models' difficulties with sports rules and complex video reasoning. Wording edits do not alter their scientific scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations of hallucinated rationale generation, camera-angle sensitivity and weak agreement between automated metrics and human judgments remain unchanged, as do the discussion and applicability qualifications.

D1.justification: The dataset repository pointer changes from haotianxia/SPORTU to chili-lab/SPORTU. Section 3.3 replaces explicit YouTube/Creative Commons provenance with a policy allowing any source subject to its copyright and license requirements. Other implementation and reproducibility details are retained.

R1.justification: The cited works, reference list and Appendix A benchmark comparison are unchanged. Positioning relative to SportQA, Sports-QA and SoccerNet-XFoul retains the same substance.

P1.justification: V4 makes limited sentence-level edits and paragraph consolidations and adds the ICLR 2025 publication header. The main section sequence and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Spacing, figure placement and pagination change, including relocation of Table 2 from page 9 to page 8. Conference running headers are added. Existing figures and tables retain their content; no displays are added or removed.

improvement.justification: The empirical evidence and appendices remain unchanged, with only limited editorial and layout gains. However, Section 3.3 removes specific YouTube/Creative Commons provenance without identifying replacement sources or licenses. This slightly weakens provenance and reuse transparency for a dataset-centered paper; the updated repository pointer does not supply those details within the PDFs.
